summary_html: Federal **Child and Family Services Reviews (CFSR)** monitor state performance on safety, permanency, and well-being. Project Milk Carton flags states that repeatedly fail or never publish CFSR improvement plans.
authority_html:
- **45 CFR Part 1355** — CFSR procedures and performance metrics  
- **Social Security Act IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — ties funding to CFSR compliance

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the court of appeals and held that the county's reasonable efforts to reunite were supported by clear and convincing evidence, explaining that reasonable efforts are assessed after statutory grounds and best interests are established.
key_cases.relevance: The reasonable-efforts findings reviewed here are the same judicial determinations the federal CFSR and IV-E reviews audit.
key_cases.quote: the appellate court then determines whether there is clear and convincing evidence that the county made reasonable efforts to reunite the family

key_cases.holding: The court held that when parental rights are terminated for palpable unfitness the district court must still determine whether reasonable efforts to rehabilitate and reunify were made, even if the determination is that services would be unrealistic.
key_cases.relevance: It makes the reasonable-efforts determination a case-by-case judicial record that federal reviewers can audit.
key_cases.quote: provision of reasonable efforts must be evaluated by the court in every case

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Children of S.E.P.
key_cases.holding: Reinstating the termination, the court held that appellate courts closely examine the record to confirm the evidence was clear and convincing, and that the findings on statutory grounds, reasonable efforts and best interests were not clearly erroneous.
key_cases.relevance: Its close review of whether case-plan services were actually delivered is the judicial counterpart to federal safety and permanency performance review.
key_cases.quote: But we closely inquire into the sufficiency of the evidence to determine whether it was clear and convincing.

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

timeline_requirements.deadline: Accepted without delay — no waiting period; if the child is determined to be missing and endangered the agency must immediately enter the child into NCIC
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Report of a missing child made to a law enforcement agency
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 299C.53; subd. 1(a) bars a law enforcement agency from refusing a missing person report because the person has been missing only a short time or because the disappearance may be voluntary.
